content: Minoxidil is a medication used to promote hair growth and slow the progression of balding. It is most effective in individuals under the age of 40 who have experienced recent hair loss. However, it does not affect receding hairlines and does not cure baldness. Any new hair growth achieved with minoxidil is typically lost within a few months after discontinuing the medication. Minoxidil is available as a liquid that is applied directly to the scalp. It is usually used twice daily. Follow the instructions provided on the packaging or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less than prescribed, and do not apply it more frequently than instructed, as exceeding the recommended dosage will not enhance or accelerate hair growth and may increase the risk of side effects. You must use minoxidil consistently for at least four months, and possibly up to one year, before observing any effects. The medication comes with three types of applicators: a metered-spray applicator for large scalp areas, an extender spray applicator (used with the metered-spray applicator) for small areas or areas under the hair, and a rub-on applicator. To use the metered-spray applicator, remove the outer and inner caps from the bottle, attach the applicator securely, and pump it six times for each dose. Avoid inhaling the mist. When not in use, place the large cap on the metered-spray bottle or the small cap on the extender spray nozzle. For the rub-on applicator, hold the bottle upright, squeeze it until the upper chamber is filled to the black line, then turn the bottle upside down and rub the medication onto the scalp. Always replace the cap when not in use. If you use your fingertips to apply the medication, wash your hands thoroughly afterward. Apply minoxidil only to dry hair and scalp. Do not apply it to other areas of the body, and avoid contact with the eyes or sensitive skin. If accidental contact occurs, rinse the area with plenty of cool water and contact your doctor if irritation develops. Do not apply minoxidil to sunburned or irritated scalp areas. Before using minoxidil, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to minoxidil or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially guanethidine (Ismelin), other blood pressure medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart, kidney, liver, or scalp diseases. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using minoxidil, contact your doctor immediately. Minoxidil may increase skin sensitivity to sunlight, so avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen. If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Minoxidil may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience scalp itching, dryness, scaling, flaking, irritation, or burning, especially if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, such as weight gain, swelling of the face, ankles, hands, or stomach, difficulty breathing (especially when lying down), rapid heartbeat, chest pain, or lightheadedness, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store minoxidil in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Minoxidil is for external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication.
